📰 News (NYT / WSJ / Bloomberg / FT / Washington Post / Economist)

items.title: The Stock Market Is Roaring. It's (Basically) All From AI.
items.desc: A WSJ midterm-coverage card argues that the stock market's recent gains are driven almost entirely by artificial intelligence. [WSJ, published 2026-11-01]

items.title: The Tangled Web of AI Bets Is Reason to Fear Tech Stocks
items.desc: Vendor financing has returned in a new form, linking AI companies' fortunes; the piece argues this magnifies the AI trade on the way up and on the way down. [WSJ, published 2026-11-01]

items.title: AI Investors Are Racing to Get Insurance on the Biggest Market Bet in History
items.desc: With trillions of dollars riding on the AI trade, investors, traders and even tech executives are looking for protection against a reversal. [WSJ, published 2026-11-01]

items.title: We're Living in the Age of the Imperial CEO
items.desc: Anthropic joins other hot tech companies in going public with a share structure that keeps founders in control. [WSJ, published 2026-11-01]

items.title: DeepSeek Drops Enhanced Coding Agent With Aim to Rival Anthropic
items.desc: DeepSeek released a prototype of a more autonomous coding agent as it seeks to challenge Anthropic's popular Claude Code. [Bloomberg, published 2026-11-01]

items.title: S. Korea Exports Extend Robust Growth as Chip Boom Continues
items.desc: South Korea's October exports kept growing strongly, underscoring an AI-driven boom that has powered its economy even as a tech-stock selloff raises doubts about the durability of the AI trade. [Bloomberg, published 2026-11-01]

items.title: AI Enthusiasm Is Collapsing and Tech Earnings Just Made It Worse
items.desc: After a run of big-tech earnings meant to clarify a wobbly market, doubts about heavy AI spending persist and the reports appear to have deepened them. [Bloomberg, published 2026-10-31]

items.title: Investors trim growth bets over fears of US economy's AI exposure
items.desc: Investors are returning to bonds after a long sell-off, as concern rises about the US economy's over-reliance on tech spending. [Financial Times, published 2026-10-31]

briefing.speaker: A
briefing.text: Hello and welcome to the Daily AI Research Digest for November first, twenty twenty-six. I'm Alex.

briefing.speaker: B
briefing.text: And I'm Sam. No new research papers on AI qualified today, so we're focusing on the news, and the theme is clear: how much the market is leaning on AI.

briefing.speaker: A
briefing.text: The Wall Street Journal says the stock market's recent roar is basically all from AI. That's a lot of concentration.

briefing.speaker: B
briefing.text: And a Journal column warns that vendor financing is back in a new form, tangling AI companies' bets together. The worry is that it magnifies the trade on the way up, and on the way down.

briefing.speaker: A
briefing.text: Related, the Journal reports that investors, traders and even tech executives are racing to buy insurance against an AI reversal, with trillions of dollars riding on it.

briefing.speaker: B
briefing.text: Bloomberg's take is blunt: AI enthusiasm is collapsing, and the latest tech earnings made it worse, because doubts about heavy AI spending haven't gone away.

briefing.speaker: A
briefing.text: The Financial Times adds that investors are trimming growth bets and returning to bonds, over fears about the US economy's exposure to AI and tech spending.

briefing.speaker: B
briefing.text: Yet the real economy is still benefiting. South Korea's October exports kept growing strongly on the chip boom, even as the selloff raises questions about how durable it is.

briefing.speaker: A
briefing.text: On the corporate side, the Journal notes Anthropic is joining other hot tech companies going public with a share structure that keeps founders in control.

briefing.speaker: B
briefing.text: And Bloomberg reports DeepSeek released a prototype of a more autonomous coding agent, aiming to rival Anthropic's Claude Code.

briefing.speaker: A
briefing.text: So: strong AI-driven activity, but growing nervousness about how much rides on it.

briefing.speaker: B
briefing.text: That's the digest. Find the full list in the web archive. Thanks for listening.
